correctness.rationale: For every prime power \(q\ge4\), the five monomials are independent: varying the nonzero \(y\)-coordinate first forces the two coefficient polynomials to vanish on all \(q-1\ge3\) nonzero \(x\)-values. The exact case partition has \(B=0\), \(2(q-1)\) nonzero torus-root-free linear polynomials \(B\), and \((q-1)^2\) linear polynomials \(B=\beta(x-r)\) with one nonzero root. Quadratic polynomials \(A\) are counted exhaustively using their distinct multiplicative roots. In the delicate case \(B=\beta(x-r)\) and \(A(r)=0\), exactly \(3(q-1)\) nonzero quotient polynomials \(Q=A/(x-r)\) have no root away from \(r\): nonzero constants and scalar multiples of \(x\) or \(x-r\). Formula coefficients sum to \(q^5\), and exact independent field arithmetic over \(\mathbb F_4,\mathbb F_5,\mathbb F_7,\mathbb F_8,\mathbb F_9\) matches each complete coefficient. The extremal support claims follow from the same exhaustive cases; generator-column geometry gives dual distance three. Finite tests corroborate, but the all-field root census supplies the proof. No claim is made for \(q\le3\) or compact-scroll full-point evaluation.

originality.rationale: The exact parameter-dependent entire Hamming enumerator for the cubic-scroll five-monomial torus code, with second minimum and geometric classification of its smallest supports, is not implied by the established dimensions, minimum distances, or dimension-five polygon equivalence classes in the materially inspected predecessor sources. Luo--Yau--Zhang--Zuo explicitly restrict their printed small-field enumerator appendix to six-dimensional codes, while the relevant scroll trapezoid is one of their five-point cases. Mathematical record searches for monomial support, scroll, Hirzebruch, enumerators, and next-weight aliases identified no equivalent finding. A highly relevant 2009 dimension-five classification could not be materially read: priority is provisionally judged under this residual risk, not certified by an unsuccessful search.

value.rationale: The fixed support is the complete hyperplane polytope of the classical smooth degree-three cubic scroll, not an arbitrary finite exponent slice. Prior theory usually supplies toric-code parameters and minimum-distance bounds; the all-prime-power full weight enumerator is a much stronger exact invariant. It determines every frequency, a sharp next weight and multiplicity, and geometric toric-fiber support classifications of extremal words. These calculations can discriminate geometrically similar codes and check code enumerators across characteristics. The result is complete, finite-dimensional yet uniform in q, not merely numerical sampling or a min-distance rederivation.
